clue.text: It's OK by us — one club or something else

definitions.text: It's OK by us — one club or something else

parts.words: It's OK by us — one club or something else
parts.note: the clue reads as approval plus a card bid, but the whole is a description of a breezy catchphrase meaning 'and there you are, all done'

explanation.walkthrough: The bridge-sounding 'one club or something else' suggests a bid; it is only whimsy around the catchphrase's casual 'whatever, it's fine' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerful catchphrase saying everything is settled and fine, which is what 'it's OK by us' expresses.

clue.text: The first decimal place is irrelevant

explanation.surface: A pedant declares that the first digit after the point does not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The first digit after the decimal point sits right next to that point; idiomatically the phrase means off the subject, not pertinent.

clue.text: The creature to exhibit saintliness

parts.note: to exhibit a quality is to be it, giving the verb BE
saintliness is being a saint, written A ST with St the usual short form of saint

explanation.surface: Someone claims an animal shows holiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'to exhibit saintliness' as 'be a St', the abbreviation for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal or brute is a creature of any kind.

clue.text: It's you' to drive, judge

explanation.surface: Someone telling a judge it is their turn to take the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'honour' in golf is the right to tee off first.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the player with the honour tees off first, so 'your honour' means you drive next; it is also how a court addresses a magistrate.

clue.text: Organization I directed with nothing to help things run smoothly

definitions.text: Organization I directed with nothing to help things run smoothly

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, the best-known international organization
nothing is zero, the letter O
directed means led, as one leads a team

explanation.surface: A manager admits running a body without any lubricant to ease its workings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: something left without lubricant to make it run smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking lubrication, with no grease applied to keep its parts moving freely.

clue.text: Wandering uselessly — not the French wanderer

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so the letters of 'uselessly' are rearranged

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Roaming without purpose, unlike some French traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' tells you to take LE (from 'the French') out of the letters of USELESSLY before rearranging the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Odysseus, under his Latin name, spent ten years roaming home from Troy, the archetypal traveller.

clue.text: Demand style

explanation.surface: Two words: insist, and fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A call is a claim or requirement, as in many calls on one's time; to call is also to name or term something.

clue.text: Finances out of order, right?

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-works
a cheque is a written order to a bank to pay money

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the money is in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' looks like a phrase about disorder, but splits into EX and an order to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The national treasury, which manages Britain's public funds.

clue.text: They control first violins

explanation.surface: The principal violinists are in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins once used to guide toddlers learning to walk; and the orchestra's principal violin section plays the top part on stringed instruments.

clue.text: It's legal to interrupt relation with an impatient exclamation

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the exclamation goes inside the other word

parts.note: a relation is an account or narrative, a story
tut is the clicking noise of impatience or disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone tutting while a relative talks is apparently within the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' suggests a relative but means a told account.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid down or required by an Act of Parliament, hence lawful.

clue.text: Cruel way to make money

indicators.note: the clue invites a way of making something out of the word cruel, by shuffling its letters

explanation.surface: A heartless method of getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy lucre is money, especially gained dishonourably.

clue.text: Foreign wife

explanation.surface: A spouse from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is London cockney for a man's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Double Dutch is foreign gibberish, and in cockney slang 'my old Dutch' is one's spouse.

clue.text: Please pay attention

explanation.surface: A polite request to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic verbs: to list is to choose or desire, as in 'the wind bloweth where it listeth', and also to hearken.

clue.text: To make repairs people need a key

parts.note: people are men in the old general sense
D is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Fixing things requires someone to hold a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a musical key, not a spanner or a door key.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix or patch up something broken.

clue.text: Nature's.in disarray, and definitively natural

indicators.note: disarray means jumbled, so the letters of 'Nature's in' are scrambled
definitively points to how 'and' ends, its final letter

explanation.surface: Nature is in chaos and is, by definition, unforced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nature's' is 'Nature is', so its S counts; 'definitively' takes the end of 'and', D.
explanation.definitionFit: Unforced and spontaneous, without effort or strain.

clue.text: Poor chap has gone spare.

parts.note: poor, as in meagre or scanty, means thin
Ned is a man's name, so a chap

explanation.surface: A hard-up man has lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone spare' is British slang for flying into a rage, but here means grown lean; the printed clue carries no letter count.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow spare is to become lean, so the word means made slimmer.

clue.text: Wearing 8, perhaps at work

explanation.surface: Dressed in 8 down, possibly while working.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading strings are a kind of harness, and to be in harness is to be at one's daily job.

clue.text: Brown paper set on fire

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to set on fire is to burn

explanation.surface: Brown wrapping paper is torched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like an adjective for paper but is the definition, a noun for a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Reddened or bronzed skin from the sun's rays, a tan.

clue.text: Part of car to wear out

explanation.surface: A car component that wears out.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipe expelling engine fumes, and to tire completely.

clue.text: Proposition put differently to her and me

indicators.note: put differently means expressed in another way, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone restates a proposal to a woman and themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement in mathematics to be proved from axioms.

clue.text: Lampoons country's flag in hiding

indicators.note: in hiding means tucked away inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: SA is South Africa, with the possessive S kept
to flag is to tire

explanation.surface: Satirical pieces mock a nation's banner that has been concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking pieces of writing ridiculing their targets.

clue.text: Conservative wearing footwear that's a disgrace

indicators.note: the footwear is worn around the letter, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a sandal is an open shoe

explanation.surface: A Tory in shoes that cause embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: A public outrage or shame.

clue.text: Hence turning into 2

indicators.note: turning means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, hence

explanation.surface: Therefore becoming the answer to 2 down.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 down is BEAST; 'turning into' looks like transformation but 'into 2' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale monster is a brute, which is what 2 down means.

clue.text: The lady's a divine creature

parts.note: the lady is her, with the 's as 'is' linking to the next piece

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'The lady's a' as HER plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek queen of the gods, wife of Zeus, a goddess.

clue.text: Prophet means to: bore in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: an auger is a tool, a means of boring holes

explanation.surface: A seer intends to bore people when talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' and 'bore' suggest intent and tedium; together they describe a drilling tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman soothsayer who foretold events from omens.

clue.text: About to enter by gate at the front

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'About to enter by gate at the front (7)' gives seven letters, but the held answer GOING has five; no parse reaches it and the true answer cannot be confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: About to enter by gate at the front

clue.text: Going the wrong way about it causes a row

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: Driving the wrong way round causes an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line or level, as in a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: One of a series of rows or levels placed one above another.

clue.text: Blemishes Juliana evidently manages to conceal

indicators.note: the words conceal the answer inside them, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Juliana covers up skin flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Birthmarks or moles, skin marks.

clue.text: Make a new plan, incorporating new standard

indicators.note: incorporating means taking inside, so one letter goes into the word

parts.note: to make a new plan is to redesign

explanation.surface: Redesigning something to include a fresh benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a level of quality but means a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag of the British merchant navy, a standard being a banner.

clue.text: Dish favoured by the top brass

explanation.surface: A meal liked by senior officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs beaten and cooked; also military slang for the gold braid on senior officers' caps.
